case_name: Bindra Devi and Ors. v. State of Himachal Pradesh and Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Himachal Pradesh and Respondent No.2 (complainant)

facts_of_case: FIR lodged against petitioners for alleged harassment; compromise between Vikas and Kalpana; petitioners seek quashing of FIR and consequential proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: Power under S. 482 CrPC is not to be exercised in cases which involve heinous and serious offences.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another (2014)6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: The power conferred under Section 482 of the Code is to be distinguished from the power which lies in the Court to compound the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: No doubt, under Section 482 of the Code, the High Court has inherent power to quash criminal proceedings even in those cases which are not compoundable and where the parties have settled the matter.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 — Sections 482 and 320

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR and consequential proceedings ordered on the basis of compromise.

use_for_drafting: quashing FIRs in domestic violence cases
